summary.text: Kevin Crutchfield is the Republican candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 34 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against Democrat April Cook.
A small business owner who served in the North Carolina House from 2023 to 2025, he won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary over incumbent Chris Measmer.

paragraphs.text: Kevin Crutchfield was born in Kingston, New York, and graduated from Owego Free Academy in 1978.
He earned an associate degree from SUNY Broome Community College in 1981 and a computer science equivalency from the University of North Carolina at Charlotte in 1992.

His career includes work as an electronic technician engineer, purchasing agent and software developer for IBM, a national sales manager for Cabarrus Plastics, and an executive at Rite Lite Signs, the Crutchfield Group and Casco Signs.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he and his wife started Casco Signs in Concord in 1998.
Crutchfield won the 2022 Republican primary and then the general election, unopposed, for North Carolina House of Representatives District 83.

He served in the House from 2023 to 2025 and was assigned to the Appropriations, Appropriations on Education, Education - Universities, Health, and Local Government - Land Use, Planning and Development committees.
He lost the 2024 Republican primary for House District 82 to Brian Echevarria.
In the 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Crutchfield listed cost of living, planning for growth in Cabarrus County and public safety as his key messages.

He said he sponsored the HOPE Act, which strengthened North Carolina's laws against human trafficking, and that state appropriations of $180 million were brought back to Cabarrus County for infrastructure.
